title: SLA Taxonomy and Credit Formula for Reserved GPU Bands (customer notice + escalation flows)
text:
SLA Taxonomy and Credit Formula for Reserved GPU Bands (customer notice + escalation flows)

description:
Purpose: Define a clear SLA taxonomy and customer-facing contract language for reserved GPU capacity ('Reserved Bands'). Provide measurable SLOs, error budget math, credit schedules, interaction rules with autoscaling, and an operational escalation flow and notification templates.

background:
Customers who purchase Reserved Bands expect predictable inference throughput and bounded latency. Current contract drafts define a high-level throughput guarantee but lack a standardized metric taxonomy, a defensible error-budget calculation, and precise notification/remediation language tied to autoscale behavior and fleet controls.

measurement_definitions:
Reserved Band: a named pool of dedicated GPUs bound to a customer with specific cardinality (e.g., 4xA100).
Provisioned Throughput (PT): the aggregate tokens-per-second capacity assigned to the Reserved Band under normal operation. Measured at the service edge by summing token-emission rate across model replicas, averaged over 1m buckets.
Observed Serve Rate (OSR): the number of user-requested tokens successfully emitted by the service per second for that customer, excluding retried/duplicated requests; measured at 1m buckets.
Serve Availability (SA): percentage of 1-minute buckets in a rolling 7-day window where OSR >= 90% of PT. Expressed as SA = (count_good_buckets / total_buckets) * 100.
95th Latency (L95): observed end-to-end 95th percentile request completion latency for generation calls (including queuing) measured over 5m windows.
Error Budget Unit (EBU): a standardized unit defined as 1% of the weekly SA target for the Reserved Band multiplied by the PT. Used to translate availability shortfalls to credit amounts.

slo_targets:
Availability SLO: SA >= 99.5% over a rolling 7-day window for production Reserved Bands (standard tier).
Burst SLO: PT must be met for sustained 5-minute windows up to aggregate burst quota; short single-minute deviations allowed without penalty if they do not reduce rolling SA.
Latency SLO: L95 <= 2800ms for sequences <= 1024 tokens measured over 24h. If model variants are used, L95 is attached to the variant used in request routing.
Failover SLO: Automatic fallback to compatible model variant in same region must occur within 30s of detected degraded replica, unless customer has disabled fallbacks.

error_budget_math:
Weekly SA Goal example: for SA target 99.5% over 7 days = 10080 minutes. Allowed failed minutes = 10080 * (1 - 0.995) = 50.4 minutes per week.
If PT=10k tokens/s and a week accrues 60 failed minutes where OSR < 90% PT, compute EBU exposure = ceil((failed_minutes / allowed_failed_minutes) * 100) percent of weekly credit pool. Credits are proportional to that percent.
Credit conversion: base_monthly_fee * (credit_percent / 100) = monetary credit. Alternatively, credits can be issued as Reserved Band time (compute-hours). The contract will default to monetary credits unless customer opts into compute-hour remediation.

credit_schedule_examples:
Minor breach (SA between 99.0%-99.49%): 5% monthly invoice credit pro rata for the affected Reserved Band for the billing period containing the breach.
Major breach (SA between 98.0%-98.99%): 15% monthly invoice credit pro rata for the affected Reserved Band.
Critical breach (SA < 98.0%): 40% monthly invoice credit pro rata, plus eligibility for a one-time remediation engineering engagement (limited to 8 engineering-hours) and the right to terminate with 30d notice and prorated refund for unused committed term.
Cumulative breach cap: credits across overlapping events for the same Reserved Band are additive but capped at 100% of the monthly fee for that band in any billing month.

contract_language_snippets:
'Service Commitment': 'Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain the Reserved Band Serve Availability (SA) at or above 99.5% measured over any rolling 7-day window. SA is defined in the measurement definitions section of this Agreement.'
'Credits': 'If Redwood fails to meet the Service Commitment in any billing period, Customer will be eligible for a Service Credit calculated in accordance with the Credit Schedule. To receive a Credit, Customer must submit a claim via the Redwood Console within 30 calendar days following the end of the billing period in which the failure occurred.'
'Exclusions': 'Service Credits will not apply where failure is caused by (a) Customer misconfiguration, (b) Customer-managed network issues, (c) force majeure, or (d) Customer request to disable fallbacks or autoscale policies that would otherwise mitigate measured impact.'
'Remedy Election': 'At Customer's election, an equivalent compute-hour remediation may be accepted in place of a monetary Credit subject to availability. Redwood's acceptance of compute-hour remediation does not waive further Customer rights under the Agreement.'

autoscale_interaction_and_fleet_controls:
Autoscale priority: Reserved Bands have a 'band priority' that gives requests from that band precedence when autoscale and burst capacity are limited. This must be documented in account configuration and cannot be escalated without contractual amendment.
Burst policy: a customer's Reserved Band can be configured with a burst window (default 120s) and burst multiple (default 2x PT). Bursts that exhaust pooled capacity are considered 'best-effort' and are excluded from SA calculations unless exhaustion triggers sustained reductions beyond allowed failed minutes.
Downscale safety: automated downscales that would drop a band's PT below guaranteed minimum must be gated by a cooldown period (15m) and operator approval if sustained for >30m, otherwise operator ticket is auto-created and customer notified.
Fleet control locks: capacity reassignments that affect a committed Reserved Band require a 48h advance scheduling window and explicit customer consent unless emergencies (safety/security) force immediate action; such emergencies are eligible for exception reporting.

operational_playbook_and_notifications:
Detection: system to auto-detect SA breaches and file internal incident ticket with 'Reserved-Band-SLA' tag and impact estimate (minutes below threshold, estimated credit percent).
Customer notification tiers: (1) Advisory - when early degradation observed (OSR trending to 90% PT for 5m); (2) Action Required - when a single 1-minute bucket drops below 80% PT or when SA drop projected to exceed allowed minutes; (3) Incident - when SA crosses breach thresholds. Templates below.
Escalation: Engineering on-call -> PM on-shift -> Customer Success -> Legal (for contract remediation) with specified SLAs for internal response times (15m, 60m, 4h respectively).
Post-incident: produce RCA within 5 business days including root cause, corrective actions, and preventive steps; include updated credit calculation and note if compute-hour remediation is offered.

customer_notification_templates:
Advisory template: 'Redwood Advisory: we have detected sustained elevated queuing affecting your Reserved Band (id: BAND-xxx). Our system shows OSR trending to 90% of Provisioned Throughput. No immediate action required; we are investigating and will provide updates. ETA for next update: 30m.'
Action Required template: 'Redwood Action Required: Your Reserved Band (id: BAND-xxx) is observing sustained reduction in Serve Rate below the configured threshold. We recommend reviewing recent model changes or enabling automatic fallback. If you would like Redwood to open an engineering investigation, reply to this thread or click the support link.'
Incident template: 'Redwood Incident: A Service Commitment breach is likely/confirmed for Reserved Band (id: BAND-xxx). We estimate affected minutes: X; expected credit percent: Y%. We will publish an RCA within 5 business days. To request an alternative remediation (compute-hour remediation), please indicate your preference in the support ticket.'

acceptance_criteria:
Legal has approved contract snippets and Credit Schedule wording.
Observability: Console shows SA, PT, OSR, and per-band credit projection in billing preview for last 30 days.
Automation: breach detection triggers internal ticket + customer notification templates fire according to defined tiers.
Billing integration: credit math flows into billing system and sample invoices show correct pro rata credits for simulated breaches.

risks_and_open_questions:
Measurement edge cases for multi-tenant GPUs where noisy neighbors cause transient PT variance — does PT include noisy neighbor headroom or is headroom excluded?
Legal: confirm preferred default for monetary credits vs compute-hour remediation and caps on cumulative credits across multiple products.
Product: define how fallbacks to cheaper variants interact with latency SLOs and whether an allowed fallback 'grace window' should be excluded from SA calculation if customer opts into it.
Operational: staffing cost to offer one-time remediation engineering engagements at scale; may require a runbook and clear acceptance criteria.

work_items_and_next_steps:
1) Draft final contract language and circulate to Legal (owner: Mateo) - due 2026-03-05.
2) Implement SA, PT, OSR telemetry panels in Console and expose historical 30d view (owner: Observability team) - scope review 2026-03-03.
3) Build breach detector + automated ticket generator and hook notification templates to the alerting pipeline (owner: Reliability) - estimate 2 sprints.
4) Billing integration spike: prototype credit application logic and e2e invoice sample (owner: Billing) - due 2026-03-18.
5) Legal/Finance signoff on credit schedule caps and compute-hour remediation rules (owner: Legal) - target 2026-03-12.
